column1: # document has, besides its value, a GRAPH: an entity index (id -> the
# tree paths that hold it) and an edge set (the checked links, each
# from one entity to one address).
# Mode `graph`, four columns; `expect` is the whole graph as JSON.
# BOTH runners additionally re-derive it on a fresh engine and require
# the same bytes: determinism is asserted as a PROPERTY here, not
# claimed in prose. It is what makes a byte-comparable golden possible
# at all -- Go map order is random, so ids, paths and edges are sorted
# by construction rather than by luck.
# G4's deliverable is that these exist and are deterministic. What is
# built on them -- impact analysis ("what reaches svc_auth?"),
# reachability, entity slices -- is a traversal, and its exposure as
# verbs and projections belongs to G7. Relation properties
# (acyclicity, inverse consistency) are phase 5's, and consume exactly
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).
# `from` is the nearest identified ANCESTOR -- the entity/component
# distinction, a node without an id being a component of the entity
# above it -- and `key` is the nearest map key below that ancestor, so
# a link inside a list is an edge under its relation rather than under
# its index. A cycle in the data is DATA: the lattice never refuses one
# (that would be non-monotone), and phase 5's checks read this set.

column3: z: id(a) & {}\ny: id(b) & {}\ns: id(s) & {dependsOn: [&: refer(), a, b]}

column1: # A checked link is stamped; a plain string that happens to look like
# an address is not, so nothing has to guess. A CLONE keeps the stamp:
# an identity says what a value IS, so a copy must not be that entity,
# but a link says what a value POINTS AT and a copy of a link points at

column3: catalog: payments: id(svc_payments) & {owner: "team-pay"}\ndeploy: eu1: payments: id(svc_payments) & {replicas: 3}

column1: # The ROOT can be the entity, and an entity can BE a link: the index
# path is `$` and the relation key is empty, because there is no key
# between the entity and the link.
# A reference to a value that IS a link clones the link, stamp and all
# — including when the clone happens after the address has resolved, so
# what travels is the resolved string rather than a residual.
# BARE id() entity sets (RELATIONS.0.md §3.1). The spread-of-type row
# is the schema idiom: the DEFINITION resolves at its own key too (a
# type body is an entity named by the schema's key), and each child at
# its own. The plain-reference row is clearing rule 1: a copy carries

column3: t: {&: id() & {kind: string}, a: {kind: k1}, b: {kind: k2}}
S: type(id() & {kind: string})\nsvcs: {&: $.S, payments: {kind: pay}, ledger: {kind: led}}

column1: # rel() EDGES: THE PREDICATE IS DECLARED, NEVER INFERRED -- it is the
# key the rel() sits on. The map-valued row is the fix the inference
# could not reach: the edge reports under `uses`, where the old
# nearest-key rule named the inner label `primary`

column3: a: id() & {}\nb: id() & {}\ns: id() & {dependsOn: rel() & [a, b]}
